title: A robot that follows a line
summary: Use reflected light to turn a line on the floor into steering decisions.
equipment: Pololu 3pi+ 32U4 robot in a configuration supported by the guide
Compatible batteries and USB cable specified by Pololu
A contrasting line course on a suitable surface
outcome: Explore the publisher’s line-following examples, calibrate reflectance sensors and observe how steering responds to the track.
stages: Meet the platform
Use the manufacturer’s guide to identify the robot version, power requirements and supported software.
Inspect the readings
Run the documented sensor examples and compare readings over the background and line before enabling movement.
Try line following
Follow the publisher’s example and calibration procedure. Begin on a simple course with room to stop.
Observe and compare
Record how curves, lighting and speed affect tracking. Change one setting at a time.
questions: What happens when the robot loses the line?
How do calibration and speed change tracking?

title: Make a servo move
summary: A small experiment connecting a software command to physical position.
equipment: Arduino-compatible board supported by the example
Power supply appropriate for the specific servo
outcome: Follow Arduino’s Sweep example and observe the relationship between commanded angle and movement.
stages: Check the components
Read the official circuit and power notes. Match the supply to your servo; requirements vary by model.
Connect the circuit
Follow the publisher’s wiring instructions with power disconnected. Keep the servo horn clear of obstructions.
Run the example
Upload the documented Sweep sketch and observe the motion.
Change the command
Experiment within your servo’s supported travel. Compare the requested position with what you can observe.
questions: Does commanding a position tell your program that the servo reached it?
What changes when the servo has a mechanical load?

title: A programmable rover
summary: An original design brief for a small rover with repeatable motion and a reliable stop.
equipment: Geared motors with encoders: selection open
Matched motor driver, controller and power system: selection open
Physical power disconnect and a clear test space
outcome: Proposed outcome: command short movements, record encoder readings and stop predictably. The component selection, wiring and software have not been validated.
stages: Define the rover
Choose payload, surface and movement limits. Record motor current, supply voltage and driver ratings before committing to parts.
Design the assembly
Model mounting points, wheel clearance and access to the power disconnect. Check the fit of the selected hardware.
Validate one subsystem
With wheels raised, verify the stop behavior, one motor direction and one encoder reading independently.
Measure a short movement
Only after subsystem checks, measure a slow straight run and compare encoder-based distance with an external measurement.
questions: Which exact components are electrically and mechanically compatible?
What should the robot do if commands stop arriving?
What evidence would make this a reproducible build guide?

title: An encoder test stand
summary: An original bench experiment for understanding speed measurement and feedback.
equipment: Low-voltage geared motor with encoder: selection open
Compatible motor driver and microcontroller: selection open
Current-limited supply matched to the selected components
Secure mount and guarded rotating parts
outcome: Proposed outcome: log measured speed, compare it with a target and investigate a basic feedback controller. No hardware configuration or controller gains have been tested.
stages: Choose compatible hardware
Document the encoder output, motor ratings and controller input limits. Establish a secure mechanical mount.
Validate measurement
Observe encoder pulses and confirm counts per revolution before computing speed.
Record open-loop behavior
Log command, elapsed time and measured speed. Keep test conditions consistent.
Explore feedback
After validating measurement and stop behavior, compare a modest proportional controller with the open-loop result. Set output limits before testing.
questions: How does sample interval affect measured speed?
How will you detect a disconnected or stalled motor?
